topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms and exact URL joining and serialization
questions: Are userinfo, query, fragment and an existing base path allowed; how many trailing slashes are removed; and what exact URL results in each case?
Are userinfo, a base path, query, fragment, malformed percent escapes, non-ASCII hosts, control characters and whitespace allowed, and exactly how are accepted forms joined and serialized?

Are user information, query, fragment, a non-root base path, encoded separators, IPv6 zone identifiers and other URL components allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the request and approval digest?

judgement.why: The URL-joining passage was unchanged, and the change did not create or affect the ambiguity.

topics.topic: Binary error-body conversion and failure-detail length measurement
questions: Is the disclosed length the original detail length, the stored truncated byte length, or a character count?
How are non-UTF-8 error-body bytes converted into failure_detail and truncated at a UTF-8 boundary?
How is a non-UTF-8 error body represented in `failure_detail`?
How is a non-UTF-8 error body converted to `failure_detail`, and is the disclosed length measured in source bytes, stored UTF-8 bytes or Unicode characters?

quotes:
The body of
   an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it
   is kept as `failure_detail`, whose class is the highest of the execution's
   class and the classes the binding declares for its outputs, under A07 rule 5.
judgement.why: The error-body-to-text and length questions already arose from this unchanged passage and were not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Credential scanning and retained detail for oversized error bodies
questions: How can the whole body be searched when it exceeds the read ceiling, and what failure_detail is retained in that case?
Is the entire potentially unbounded body streamed and searched, or is only the prefix read up to `service_response_bytes_max` searched?
If an oversized error body contains the credential only after the read ceiling, must the detail be withheld, and how can that be determined without reading the whole body?

quotes: status 3xx or 5xx, whatever the body's size — reading stops at the ceiling

Before anything is kept, the whole body is searched for the bytes of the
   credential value sent with the request;
judgement.why: One passage stops reading at the ceiling while the other requires searching the whole body.

topics.topic: Filesystem paths and operations available directly to sandboxed agent code
questions: May agent code itself read or write arbitrary paths in the exchange directory or read files from the runtime, or are those paths accessible only to the runner?
May function code read and write arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner's input/output machinery?
Which filesystem paths and operations may agent code itself use, as opposed to paths used only by the trusted runner?

quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
judgement.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Meaning and enforcement of deterministic execution
questions: Is deterministic output a guaranteed sandbox property, an admission test that may detect only observed differences, or merely an expectation of authored code?
Which remaining nondeterministic observations are forbidden or normalized, and how is that enforced?
Is deterministic output a guaranteed sandbox property, or only an expectation tested for selected implementations?

quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
judgement.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Multipart boundary generation, byte-level encoding, and approval identity
questions: How is the multipart boundary selected, and may a resend of the same approved description use different request bytes solely because its boundary differs?
Does changing multipart boundary bytes invalidate an approval, and must the boundary be fixed before approval?
What exact multipart encoding is sent, including boundary generation, CRLF placement, quoting and terminal delimiter?

quotes:
The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: The multipart approval-description rule was unchanged, and the change did not affect boundary selection or serialization.

topics.topic: Required authored trial-case keys and whether expected outputs may be partial
questions: May an authored case specify expected values for only some outputs, and if so are unspecified outputs ignored or merely required to validate?
What exact key set must authored `inputs` and present `expected_outputs` contain?
May an authored case specify only some expected outputs, and if so which outputs participate in `output_mismatch`?

judgement.why: The authored trial-case key-set question concerns unchanged text and was not affected by the change.

topics.topic: Whether every mechanism for observing clock time must be prohibited
questions: Is the finite list the complete prohibition, or must every other way of observing time also be denied?
Are omitted clock APIs usable, or must every clock-observing API be trapped?
Are these omitted time sources allowed, or must they also be unavailable to function code?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The completeness of the clock-trap list was already at issue in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Allowed HTTP header values and wire encoding of non-ASCII characters
questions: How are non-ASCII header values encoded on the wire, or must all configured header values be ASCII?
Which exact characters and bytes are valid in required and credential header values, and how are accepted Unicode values encoded on the wire?

judgement.why: Exact header character grammars and wire encodings are contract and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Cached state and retry behavior after a failed configuration or token reload
questions: What digest and token-list state is retained after a failed re-read, and how is recovery to previously valid identical content detected?
After a failed re-read, what state is cached and what condition forces later requests to parse the configuration again?

quotes:
Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ,
   or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it (K-15) and takes from it only the
   token list.
judgement.why: The cached-digest recovery question concerns this unchanged passage; adding the duplicate-agent-name check did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Canonical ordering of tied edges and constants for identity and proof checks
questions: How are tied edges and constants ordered before hashing and while selecting the first proof failure?
Which such edge is considered first for guard failures, and how can reordered equal-key edges retain the same `flow_version_id`?
How are tied edges and constants ordered before hashing, so equivalent submissions cannot receive different identities?

quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
judgement.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Classification and failure ordering for malformed or ambiguous manifests
questions: Are duplicate member names anywhere in a manifest record a manifest mismatch, and where do they fall in rule 5's failure order?
How are absent and duplicate selected-instance entries classified at proposal, acceptance and send time?
How are every malformed manifest shape and type classified, and where do those checks occur in the first-failure order?

judgement.why: Manifest field shapes, types, and duplicate-member handling are schema and contract closure matters for State 6.

topics.topic: Classification and size-limit precedence for uncanonicalizable returned values
questions: How is an uncanonicalizable returned value counted and classified?
What outcome wins when an invalid output cannot be canonicalized or byte-counted?

quotes:
The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every
   `value` output and the bytes of every `file` output of the one call of `run` —
   for a `many` file output, the sum of its elements' bytes.
judgement.why: The counting of uncanonicalizable outputs was already unresolved by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Definition and enforcement of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: What hosts qualify for the loopback exception, and must the connected address also be loopback?
Is loopback determined from a literal IP in the URL, from DNS resolution, or from the actual connected address, and how are mixed or changing DNS answers handled?

quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
judgement.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Durable classification and reconstruction of mapped value-list overflow
questions: What exact node conclusion is derived, how is it reproduced after restart, and what failure reason appears in the trace and run result?
What durable fact records that the mapped node failed because its aggregate list was too large, and what exact conclusion/status is reconstructed after restart?

judgement.divergence: One implementation can recompute aggregate overflow after restart and keep the mapped node failed; another can reconstruct only the successful element records and treat the mapped node as successful. The run caller and downstream nodes observe different run status, execution, and outputs.
judgement.why: The new aggregate-overflow rule supplies no durable failure fact or exact reconstructed conclusion.

topics.topic: Durable storage of disclosure classes for many-file references
questions: Where is the class of a non-empty many-file reference durably represented so it can be reconstructed and redacted after restart?
Where is the disclosure class of an empty `many` file reference durably recorded so it can be recovered and disclosed after restart?

quotes:
`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty
    list keeps the class A13 rule 6 gives it and counts in an execution's
    class (A07 rule 5).
judgement.why: The later contract explicitly stores the class on the file-list reference, including an empty list.

topics.topic: Escaping and validity rules for port names in multipart headers
questions: Which port names are allowed, or how are quotes, backslashes, CR/LF and non-ASCII characters escaped in multipart headers?
How are quotes, backslashes, controls, non-ASCII characters and line breaks in port names handled in multipart headers?

quotes:
Each part has exactly two
   headers: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with
   `filename="<port>"` added for a file part, and `Content-Type`, the port's
   media type for a file part and `application/json` for a value part, without
   parameters; nothing else.
judgement.why: Multipart port-name escaping was already unresolved by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Event establishing total order among concurrent requests
questions: What establishes the total order when requests are received concurrently?
What event establishes the total order of concurrent requests?

quotes:
Surface requests are
   handled one at a time in the order they arrive: one request, including the run
   advancement it causes (A13), ends before the next begins, so an approval, a
   cancellation and a resume of one run never race.
judgement.why: The arrival-order question concerns unchanged concurrency text and was not affected by the change.

topics.topic: Filesystem ownership, type, permission, ACL, and symlink checks for private data
questions: What ownership, file-type and mode checks are required for the directory, database, value area, fixtures and spool entries?
What exact filesystem ownership, permission, ACL and symlink checks decide whether startup is allowed?

quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
judgement.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Handling and bounding of function stdout and stderr
questions: Are stdout and stderr discarded, bounded, redirected into the scratch limit, or treated as output/resource exhaustion?
What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr?

quotes:
Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel. The kernel keeps
   at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it as `failure_detail`, and only for the
   exception type and message, never stdout.
judgement.why: The handling of stdout and stderr was already left open by this unchanged rule.

topics.topic: Reliable detection and classification of resource-limit violations
questions: What observable conditions prove that each resource limit was hit rather than that the process merely crashed?
How does the kernel reliably detect a caught memory or process-count limit hit and distinguish it from an ordinary exception or successful return?

quotes:
Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds
   deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count,
   scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised —
   `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the
   process exited abnormally — `crashed`;
judgement.why: Reliable detection distinguishing a limit hit from a crash was already required by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Store ordering of records created within one atomic transaction
questions: How are records within one transaction positioned relative to each other for activation identity, paging, oldest-first recovery and oldest matching approval?
What is the store-order sequence for records created atomically together, including outputs, NodeExecution, TrialExecutions, verdicts and activations?

quotes:
The kernel is one process with one store and one writer. A change is one call in
one transaction inside the store module; callers do not open, name or pass
transactions.
judgement.why: The relative order of multiple records in one transaction was already unresolved and the change did not create that issue.

topics.topic: TLS verification policy and trust store
questions: What exact verification policy determines whether an HTTPS pre-send connection is allowed?
What exact TLS verification policy and trust store must every implementation use?

quotes: TLS is verified for `https`.
judgement.why: The exact TLS verification policy was already unspecified by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Accepted media-type grammar and canonical comparison
questions: What media-type grammar is accepted, are parameters allowed, and how is comparison canonicalized?

topics.topic: Authority required to resume an unreachable read operation
questions: What authority check applies when resuming an unreachable `read` operation?

topics.topic: Behavior on content-digest collision or corrupted existing content
questions: What does the kernel do on a digest collision or corrupted existing content?

topics.topic: Canonical data structure used to compute approval request_digest
questions: What exact canonical data structure produces request_digest?

topics.topic: Canonical value structure hashed for an operation idempotency key
questions: Is the hashed value an object keyed by field name, a list in manifest order, or a scalar when there is one field?

topics.topic: Classification and attempt creation for local HTTP request-construction failures
questions: How is a local request-construction or HTTP-client rejection classified, and does it create an EffectAttempt?

topics.topic: Classification and shutdown behavior for a symlink discovered during a run
questions: Does this become internal_error followed by the A14 shutdown, a node failure, or an ordinary refusal?

topics.topic: Disposition of outcome_unknown attempts when another approval is refused
questions: If another branch has an outcome_unknown attempt when an approval is refused, does that attempt remain unknown permanently, become otherwise classified, or remain owner-resolvable despite the ended run?

topics.topic: Events represented by live NodeExecution start and end timestamps
questions: For an operation attempt, are started_at and ended_at the request-build times, first-byte/final-response times, or EffectAttempt recorded/concluded times?

topics.topic: Exact trailing newline removal rule for credentials
questions: Does this remove LF only, one CRLF pair, either one line ending, or exactly one final Unicode newline; and what happens with two trailing line endings?

topics.topic: GET and DELETE binding validity across cardinalities and schema types
questions: How do port cardinality and schema type combine when deciding whether a GET or DELETE binding is valid, particularly for a `many` port whose element schema is itself `array` or `null`?

topics.topic: Handling of missing or non-string manifest idempotency_key values
questions: How are missing, numeric, object, array or boolean `idempotency_key` values handled for read and non-read operations?

topics.topic: Meaning and enforcement timing of JSON Schema on file ports
questions: What does a JSON Schema on a file port validate, and when can a file fixture or output fail that schema?

topics.topic: Observable constant-time requirement for token comparison
questions: What observable timing property must authentication preserve?

topics.topic: Ordering of kernel startup validation checks
questions: In what order are configuration, token, data-directory, manifest-dependent credential-header, store-lock and sandbox checks performed?

topics.topic: Proposal-time handling of operation bindings with unsupported schemas
questions: Must an operation binding with an unsupported schema be refused at proposal time?

topics.topic: Recorded outcome, committed state, and caller response when cleanup fails
questions: If cleanup fails after a timeout, resource exhaustion or sandbox violation, which outcome is recorded?
What is returned to the caller, and which enclosing records are committed, before the process stops?

topics.topic: Required HTTP version and exact protocol serialization rules
questions: What HTTP version and serialization rules must the invoker use to make the promised wire request exact?

topics.topic: Resolution and immutability requirements for manifest_revision
questions: How is manifest_revision resolved, and must it be an immutable commit rather than a mutable branch, tag or directory state?

topics.topic: Size limits and refusal behavior for durable previews and outbound metadata
questions: What limits apply to manifest/configuration/secret files and to each URL, header and resulting approval preview, and what refusal occurs when a limit is exceeded?

topics.topic: Standing-grant target validity and refusal-check ordering
questions: Is granting a function node refused, and in what order are active-version, node-existence, node-kind, destructive-class and already-active-grant checks made?

topics.topic: Timestamps assigned to nodes that are not executed
questions: What timestamps do skipped, upstream-failed and pre-input-validation records receive?

topics.topic: Whether admitted implementations remain valid after a kernel release upgrade
questions: After upgrading the kernel release, may an already admitted implementation continue serving without being admitted under the new runtime?

topics.topic: Whether file or many inputs may bind to path placeholders
questions: May a file input or a `many` input be bound to a path placeholder?

topics.topic: Wire and service semantics when a null idempotency field is omitted
questions: May an effect's idempotency-key field be omitted from the wire because its value is null, and if so what idempotency value does the service receive?
